subject: Transient tokenization tail causing p95/p99 lift — mitigation runbook & customer note
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Observed p95/p99 lift on gen-api for Parcelly (early alert)

Team —

Seeing a sustained p95/p99 lift on gen-api for the last ~25 minutes for the Parcelly production key (PL-2027-311). Symptoms: tokenization stage occasionally takes 300–800ms (baseline ~25ms) for some requests, which cascades into throughput collapse on our pooled inference lanes. Overall token throughput for their tenant dropped ~40% and queueing increased.

Initial notes:
- Impact window: ~08:50–09:10 UTC, intermittent after 09:05.
- Affected path: /v1/generate (non-streaming, short prompts)
- Customer traffic pattern: steady query rate; nothing obvious from their headers.

Asking SRE/infra to triage tokenization hotspot and Eng for quick mitigations we can push (routing rules / model fallback). Aditya, can Product weigh in on temporary config options we can expose? Marissa/Rachel — I'm going to draft a customer note once we have a short mitigation and ETA.

Attaching request tracker: I'll collect CPU profiles and heap snapshots if SRE wants them.

—Diego
Diego Fernandez
Product Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 10:05:42 -0000
Subject: Re: Observed p95/p99 lift on gen-api for Parcelly (early alert)

Diego —

Thanks for the heads-up. We're seeing the same in infra telemetry: elevated syscalls in the tokenization worker and increased context-switches for the tokenizer process on the GPU host pool serving Parcelly. Initial triage:

- Collected CPU samples (attached cpu-profiles.zip) and a short perf trace from two affected hosts.
- Hypothesis: a rare codepath in our unicode normalization step is hitting pathological input (very long multi-codepoint clusters from non-standard punctuation), forcing an O(N^2) path in tokenizer C++.
- Action items (SRE): throttle request concurrency for Parcelly on the affected lane and enable the per-tenant fallback routing that sends new requests to quantized-encoder variants.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
SRE Lead — Serving Reliability

Attachments: cpu-profiles.zip
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 11:30:15 -0000
Subject: Re: Observed p95/p99 lift on gen-api for Parcelly (early alert)

Quick product / roadmap context:

- We have a short-term knob we can flip: per-tenant tokenizer fallback to a simpler normalization path (less accurate on rare unicode sequences but deterministic and O(N)). It exists as an internal feature flag but is not exposed in the console yet. Engineering estimate to make it a safe runtime toggle: ~2–3 engineer-days for QA and a canary rollout.
- Medium-term: we planned a tokenizer robustness effort in Q2 (INF-9128) that hardens edge cases — doesn't help this hour.

Ask from Product: If SRE can validate that the fallback removes the CPU spike without significantly increasing tokenization errors, Product can green-light a controlled flag flip for Parcelly and add monitoring. Also: we should scope if this becomes a per-model opt-in vs a per-tenant routing rule.

Aditya
Aditya Rao
Product Manager — Model Serving
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 14:40:03 -0000
Subject: Re: Observed p95/p99 lift on gen-api for Parcelly (early alert)

Looping in Customer Success & comms. Drafted a short customer note below and dropped a markdown file (parcelly-cust-note-draft.md) in the incident folder. Please review — we need a one-paragraph explanation + next steps and an ETA for mitigation.

Draft (please edit / sign-off):
Hi Lena —

Thanks for flagging the elevated latency this morning. Our engineering team identified an intermittent tokenizer processing path that produced longer-than-normal CPU spikes for a small subset of inputs. We have applied a targeted routing workaround that sends new requests from Parcelly to a validated fallback tokenizer to reduce the latency impact. You may see slightly different tokenization behavior on rare punctuation-heavy prompts; we do not expect this to change model output quality materially.

Next steps: we will continue collecting traces, push a config toggle today (if SRE confirms), and provide an ETA for the permanent fix within 72 hours. We'll also share a short post-incident note once the root cause is fixed.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Operations

Attachments: parcelly-cust-note-draft.md
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 08:10:22 -0000
Subject: Re: Observed p95/p99 lift on gen-api for Parcelly (early alert)

Update —

SRE ran the targeted routing and enabled the quantized-encoder fallback for the Parcelly tenant at 2027-02-10T15:28:00-05:00. Early results: p95 has dropped from ~820ms to ~120–160ms across the affected pool, throughput has recovered to ~95% of baseline. There are a handful of prompts that still show higher tokenization time; we're continuing to gather traces.

Two immediate asks:
1) Product: please confirm we can flip the internal tokenizer flag for this tenant for the next 48–72 hours while we complete a small QA pass (Aditya). If yes, Marissa will send the customer note.
2) Eng/SRE: can we preserve the capture of one sample per minute for the affected pool until the root cause is closed (Jira INF-9128)? That trace retention will be useful for debugging.

If all agree, I'll send a short customer update by 09:30 UTC.

—Diego

Hi Lena —

Quick update from Redwood: our engineering team identified an intermittent tokenizer processing path that affected a small percentage of your requests earlier this morning. We applied a targeted routing change that sends new requests to a validated fallback tokenizer while we finish our investigation. Early measurements show significant latency improvement and throughput has mostly recovered.

What to expect now:
- Slight, rare changes in tokenization behavior on punctuation-heavy prompts; expected downstream model outputs should remain equivalent for the majority of cases.
- We'll provide a detailed incident follow-up within 72 hours, including any compensating measures if we find output regressions.

If you notice anything else or want to coordinate a quick call to walk through traces, let me know and we can schedule.

Thanks for your patience — we'll keep you posted.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
Parcelly account lead
